exposure: Intracranial hemorrhage location (infratentorial, infra- and supratentorial, infra- and supratentorial + parenchymal involvement)
Mode of delivery (spontaneous vaginal delivery, vacuum extraction, caesarean section)
Infra- and supratentorial + parenchymal involvement haemorrhage
cohort: 240 infants born at 34 weeks' gestation or more
finding: Mild intracranial haemorrhage is relatively common in late preterm and term infants, often as an incidental finding in asymptomatic babies, while early neurological symptoms appear to be related to parenchymal involvement.
mod_finding: Uncomplicated spontaneous vaginal delivery was reported in 20/36 neonates (56%), vacuum extraction in 4 (11%) and caesarean section in 12 (33%).
